network_binding.rationale: OpenCode serve mode must not be exposed on LAN or WAN. The steward and workers communicate with the serve instances over localhost TCP. This is a hard safety requirement — no remote code execution surface.

port_allocation.strategy: sequential allocation from a base port range, with collision detection before bind. Each session gets a distinct port. Ports are recorded in the session ledger and released on session teardown.

auth_policy.password_policy: Use OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD only when serve mode is actually implemented in v2. The v1 streaming serverless mode does not use serve mode at all. Do not set or reference this env var in v1 code.
auth_policy.rationale: The password is an implementation detail of serve mode. Prematurely introducing it creates a latent credential that must be scrubbed from env, logs, and telemetry.

startup_sequence: steward scans ports to find available base port
steward starts its own OpenCode serve instance on allocated port
steward starts worker-0 serve instance on next port
steward starts worker-1 serve instance on next port
steward starts reviewer serve instance on next port
steward writes session ledger entry for each started session
steward begins scan cycle (roadmap queue → assign → monitor)

lane_lease.description: A lane lease assigns a roadmap lane (task) to a specific worker. Only the steward can create lane leases. A lane lease is exclusive — at most one worker holds the lease for a given lane at any time.

path_lease.description: A path lease reserves a file path (or directory) for a specific worker. Created by the steward during lane assignment. Workers must check path leases before writing. Collisions are detected by the steward on scan.

transitions: pending → active (steward assigns work to worker)
active → completed (worker finishes lane and writes report)
active → revoked (steward detects misbehavior or collision)
active → conflict (steward detects path collision with another worker)

assignment_policy.who_assigns: Only the steward session assigns work. The steward reads the roadmap queue, classifies tasks, selects safe non-blocked tasks, and creates lane leases and path leases for worker sessions.
rules: A worker may only hold one active lane lease at a time
A worker may hold multiple path leases (one per file in allowed_files)
Path leases must not overlap between active workers
The steward must revoke leases on worker heartbeat timeout
The reviewer may recommend lease revocation but cannot execute it

mission_packets.format: one JSON file per mission, named {worker_id}-{lane_id}.json

worker_reports.format: one JSON file per completed mission, named {worker_id}-{lane_id}-report.json

operating_picture.format: single aggregated JSON, regenerated each scan cycle

heartbeat_model.format: append-only JSONL entry to sessions ledger with event=heartbeat, worker_id, timestamp, status
actions_on_timeout: steward marks worker session as 'lost' in session ledger
steward revokes all active leases held by the lost worker
steward reassigns the lost worker's lane to the reviewer session as spare
if reviewer session is already occupied, steward halts with safety stop 'all_workers_lost'

allowed_formats: structured JSON artifacts conforming to known schemas
content-light summaries with path hashes only
ingestion_pipeline: steward reads report projections (not raw reports) on scan cycle
steward correlates report paths with active lane leases
steward updates operating picture with plugin-derived insights
raw plugin output never enters worker mission packets

ownership_model.granularity: file path level, with directory-level awareness for collections
ownership_model.lease_type: path lease per file in allowed_files, plus implicit exclusivity on the lane
ownership_model.conflict_definition: Two active path leases conflict if they reference the same path or if one path is a descendant of another leased directory

detection.on_assign: steward checks all active path leases before creating new leases for a lane assignment
detection.during_work: workers check path leases before every file write; steward re-scans active leases on each scan cycle
detection.on_report: steward validates that worker report paths match assigned path leases

resolution.conflict_response: Steward revokes the newer lease and halts the affected worker. The lane is reassigned to the reviewer session if available.
resolution.escalation: If the reviewer session is occupied, steward halts with safety stop 'unresolvable_path_collision' and emits an audit_unblock_plan.

test_coordination.test_scope_per_worker: Each worker runs only the targeted_tests specified in its mission packet. The steward ensures no two workers run overlapping test suites on the same files simultaneously.
test_coordination.coordination_protocol: Before assigning a lane with targeted_tests, the steward checks whether any other worker holds a path lease on files that the tests would exercise. If so, the assignment is deferred until the conflicting worker completes or the lease expires.

final_report_fan_in.collection: Steward reads all worker report artifacts from .rig/opencode/worker_reports/ at the end of each scan cycle.
final_report_fan_in.merge_strategy: Steward merges worker reports by lane_id, preserving per-lane content-light summaries, path hashes, and test results. No raw file content or chat transcripts are included.

output.format: single JSON artifact conforming to rig.relay.opencode_pool_report.v1

audit_unblock_handoff.trigger: Steward classifies state as 'audit_unblock_plan' (no safe non-blocked work available).
audit_unblock_handoff.handoff_artifact: Steward writes opencode_idle_steward_unblock_audit_v1.json to the build directory, and emits an unblock_candidate event for each blocked task.
audit_unblock_handoff.reviewer_action: Reviewer reads the audit, validates blocker classifications, reviews recommended unblock slices, and either approves (queues the unblock work) or amends (writes amended recommendations).
audit_unblock_handoff.feedback_loop: If the reviewer amends, the steward reads the amended audit and re-evaluates. If the reviewer approves, the steward queues the unblock slices as new roadmap items and resumes scan cycle.

redaction_rules: Raw prompt text never stored in mission packets or worker reports
Raw model chain-of-thought never stored in canonical evidence; always redacted in event records
Raw file contents never stored in session, lease, or report artifacts
File paths are stored with SHA-256 hashes as the canonical identifier
stderr is truncated to 4KB and hashed before storage
OpenCode serve-mode auth tokens never stored in any artifact
Worker session passwords generated per-session and never persisted to disk
content_light_guarantees: Mission packets contain: lane_id, title, agent, allowed_files (paths + hashes), forbidden_files, targeted_tests, completion_criteria, bounded prompt summary (not raw prompt)
Worker reports contain: lane_id, worker_id, exit_code, duration_ms, paths_changed (hashes only), test_results (pass/fail counts, no raw output), bounded summary, stderr_sha256
Session ledger contains: session_id, worker_id, role, port, status, started_at, last_heartbeat_at — no passwords, no tokens, no raw output
Lease ledger contains: lease_id, path_sha256, worker_id, lane_id, status, timestamps — no raw file contents
Operating picture contains: worker statuses, active lane counts, blocked lane counts, collision counts, heartbeat health — aggregated, not raw

hard_stops: all_workers_lost — all worker sessions have timed out and reviewer is already occupied; pool cannot make progress
unresolvable_path_collision — two active path leases conflict and neither can be safely revoked
steward_session_lost — steward heartbeat monitor detects its own session is unhealthy (external watchdog)
serve_port_conflict — a required port is already in use at startup
lease_ledger_corruption — lease ledger is unreadable or contains conflicting entries
soft_stops: reviewer_occupied — reviewer session is already handling a review and a new unblock_audit is generated
single_worker_remaining — only one worker is healthy; steward may continue but with reduced parallelism
high_heartbeat_latency — heartbeats are arriving but with >50% of timeout window consumed
recovery: Hard stops require human operator intervention. Pool writes a safety_stop event with reason and context.
Soft stops are logged and the steward may continue in degraded mode.
After any stop, the steward writes an audit_unblock_plan capturing the pool state at halt time.

reasons: Streaming serverless mode (subprocess.Popen) is simpler to implement, test, and verify than a four-session serve-mode pool
A single-run streaming steward exercises the content-light event model, reasoning redaction, stderr capture, and path hashing — all of which are prerequisites for multi-worker mode
The serve-mode pool requires session lifecycle management, port allocation, heartbeat monitoring, and lease coordination — each of which is a non-trivial subsystem
Implementing streaming serverless mode first surfaces integration issues (OpenCode JSON format, event types, error handling) before adding the complexity of multi-worker coordination
The content-light doctrine and redaction rules must be battle-tested on a single streaming run before scaling to four concurrent sessions
Dry-run mode remains the default for tests; streaming is a new capability that must not regress the existing classification-only steward
preconditions_for_v2: Streaming serverless mode is stable and passing all existing + new tests
Content-light event record schema is validated and redaction rules are proven
Path hashing and stderr truncation boundaries are tuned based on real OpenCode runs
The single-run steward handles all OpenCode event types (step_start, reasoning, text, tool_use, step_finish, error) correctly
Terminal progress display is usable and --show-reasoning-stream works as designed
Environment sanitization is verified against the full sensitive env var blocklist

steward_context_capsule.description: The steward context capsule is the integration seam between worker evidence and steward decision inputs. Workers write structured evidence artifacts; the context compiler/assembler digests them into a content-light operating-picture capsule; the steward consumes the capsule and remains the dispatch authority.

capsule_artifact.format: single JSON file, regenerated each scan cycle

compilation_rules: Workers write structured evidence artifacts to .rig/opencode/worker_reports/
The context compiler digests worker reports, lease ledger, and dirty state into a unified capsule
The capsule contains normalized decision inputs: task counts, blocker summaries, completion criteria status, gate status, recommended action
The capsule is content-light — no raw prompt text, no raw model chain-of-thought, no raw file contents
File paths are stored as SHA-256 hashes only
The compiler may recommend continue_lane, finalize_lane, advance_to_next_lane, blocked, or audit_unblock_plan
The steward consumes the capsule and remains the policy and dispatch authority — it may override compiler recommendations
If the capsule is missing or invalid, the steward falls back to narrowly required local evidence reads and records the fallback in its run artifact
The compiler must never directly launch OpenCode — only the steward launches workers
Plugins must never directly invoke the context compiler with raw chat transcripts
worker_to_capsule_pathway: Worker completes mission → writes worker_report to .rig/opencode/worker_reports/{worker_id}-{lane_id}-report.json
Worker report contains: exit_code, duration_ms, paths_changed (hashes only), test_results (pass/fail counts), bounded summary, stderr_sha256
Context compiler reads all available worker reports on scan cycle
Context compiler aggregates worker status into active_lane_summary in the capsule
Context compiler updates completion_criteria_status from worker reports
Capsule may drive static docs/UI and cockpit projections in future iterations
evidence_graph_relationships: lease_summary → explains why files are reserved and by which worker
gate_status → explains why a lane is blocked on missing/failed gates
completion_criteria_status → explains why a lane is complete or incomplete
unresolved_seams → lists missing artifacts and reports that block progress
recommended_action + recommendation_rationale_codes → machine-readable decision trail from compiler to steward

artifacts.purpose: Session ledger recording every session in the pool: creation, heartbeat, status changes, teardown
Lease ledger recording every lane and path lease: creation, assignment, completion, expiration, revocation
Per-mission packets containing the bounded prompt, allowed files, targeted tests, and completion criteria for each worker assignment
Per-worker per-mission reports containing exit code, duration, paths changed (hashes), test results (counts), and bounded summary
Derived operating picture regenerated each scan cycle: worker statuses, active lane counts, collision counts, heartbeat health, pool state summary
